learning_outcomes.text: Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to metrology
The humanity and measurements
Division of metrology: scientific, industrial and legal
Organization of metrology: international infrastructure and regional metrological organizations
National metrology institutes (NMI)
Fundamentals of metrology
Metrological terms and concepts
International System of Units (SI). Magnitudes and units
Measurement standards: dissemination of basic magnitudes. Calibration and traceability
Uncertainty Evaluation
Basic concepts: measurement, errors, effects, corrections, influence quantities
Evaluation of typical uncertainty: measurement model, type A and type B evaluation
Evaluation of combined uncertainty: without correlation and with correlation
Evaluation of expanded uncertainty: coverage factor, expression of uncertainty
Metrology in the area of length
Classification of instruments and standards. Analysis of metrological characteristics
Direct and indirect measurements with dimensional, angular, form and surface quality instruments
Calibration procedures
Coordinate metrology
Organization of metrological laboratories
ISO 17025 standard. Quality assurance in a laboratory
Ensuring traceability: calibration plan and comparisons
Measurement and calibration capability
Laboratory accreditation
Introduction to quality control and total quality systems
Introduction, concepts of quality and quality control
Evolution of quality control
Benefits of quality control and total quality systems
Costs associated with quality: types and estimation
Quality management: management practices, tools for quality improvement and ISO 9000 standard
Process control methods
Control charts for variables
Creation of control charts for variables
Modified control charts
Interpretation of control charts for variables
Control charts for attributes
Creation of control charts for attributes
Determination of process capability. Continuous control
Acceptance control
Acceptance control plans by attributes
Characteristic curve of a sampling plan. Properties
Sampling procedures
Regulations
teaching_methods: Resolution of problems and practical cases
assessment_rules: For progressive evaluation, the final grade C = 0.05 · mpl1 + 0.05 · mpl2 + 0.05 · mpl3 + 0.10 · mti + 0.375 · epa1 + 0.375 · epa2. To pass, students must attend all lab practices, obtain at least 4.5/10 in each partial exam, and achieve a final grade C >= 5/10. For global evaluation, C = PL + TI + 0.375 · epa1 + 0.375 · epa2, where PL (lab practices) and TI (individual work) grades are the maximum of submitted reports or specific exams. The same minimum requirements for attendance and partial exam scores apply for global evaluation to pass. In the extraordinary (resit) exam, the final grade is 100% determined by a single written exam, requiring attendance to lab practices and a minimum of 5/10 in the exam.
